title: The Dyatlov Pass case
hook: In 1959, nine hikers walked into the Ural Mountains. None of them came back.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: Their tent stood on the slope of Kholat Syakhl, a name meaning Dead Mountain.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: When rescuers arrived, the tent was still there, cut open from the inside.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Footprints led downhill, some barefoot, some in socks, in minus thirty degrees.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Some had crushed ribs and a fractured skull, yet no wounds on the skin.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: Soviet investigators closed the case, blaming an unknown compelling natural force.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: In 2021, scientists showed a small slab avalanche could explain the injuries. But not why they fled.

end.line: So what really happened on Dead Mountain?

description: Nine experienced hikers died on a Ural mountainside in 1959, and their tent was cut open from the inside. The Dyatlov Pass case is still argued about today.

facts.claim: Nine hikers led by Igor Dyatlov died in the northern Urals in early February 1959.
facts.source: Wikipedia: Dyatlov Pass incident; Russian Prosecutor General 2020

facts.claim: Kholat Syakhl means Dead Mountain in the Mansi language.
The tent was found cut open from the inside; footprints led downhill, some in socks or barefoot.
Temperatures that night were around minus 25 to minus 30 °C.
Several victims had chest fractures and one a fractured skull, without external wounds.
The 1959 inquiry concluded the deaths were caused by an unknown compelling natural force.
In 2021 Gaume and Puzrin modelled a small slab avalanche that could explain the injuries.
